title: Flat restriction of scalars preserves K-injectives
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings such that for every
scheme $X$ the extension of scalars $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$ preserves finite limits
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]). Then for every scheme $X$ the restriction of scalars
$\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\colon\Mod_{\Lambda'_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ sends K-injective complexes
([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]) to K-injective complexes.

proof.text: Fix a scheme $X$ and put $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, using a small representative in the chosen universe. The abelian-category clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] makes $\mathcal C$ abelian; its assertion about injectives is not needed. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], this category is closed symmetric monoidal and tensoring on either side preserves colimits. In particular tensoring preserves the zero object and binary coproducts, hence the biproduct addition formula $f+g=\nabla\circ(f\oplus g)\circ\Delta$, so tensoring is additive. Equalizers and coequalizers exist in an abelian category (as kernels and cokernels of differences). The map $a_X:\Lambda_X\to\Lambda'_X$ is a morphism of commutative ring objects by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Thus all hypotheses of clauses 2, 3 and 4 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] hold. These clauses give abelian categories $\mathcal B=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ and $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda'_X}$, an adjunction $E=\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}\dashv R=\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$, and preservation of finite colimits by $E$.

source.place: proof paragraph, Ext–Res adjunction and right exactness; ambient abelianness: Stacks tag 03CN, sites-modules.tex, lemma-abelian-abelian (1)

proof.text: Restriction $R$ is additive: it leaves underlying morphisms unchanged by clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], and sums of module morphisms are their underlying sums. Extension $E$ is additive because it preserves finite coproducts and the zero object: finite coproducts in an abelian category are biproducts, their projections are characterized using identities and zero maps, and the biproduct formula $f+g=\nabla\circ(f\oplus g)\circ\Delta$ is therefore preserved. The hypothesis on $a$ gives preservation of finite limits by $E$ at this particular $X$. Together with the finite-colimit preservation from step 1, this is exactly exactness as defined in [def-galois-exact-functor] (Stacks tag 0034, definition-exact).

source.place: proof paragraph, exactness of extension; Stacks tag 0034, categories.tex, definition-exact

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $u=R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $v=E:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. Step 1 supplies the abelian categories and $v\dashv u$, and step 2 supplies additivity and exactness of $v$. The cited theorem then says that applying $R$ termwise to every K-injective complex $I$ in $\mathcal A$ produces a K-injective complex in $\mathcal B$, which is the required assertion at $X$. Since $X$ was arbitrary, the assertion holds for every scheme. This is the source's argument packaged by the existing generic theorem; no boundedness of $I$ is required.
